_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Mathematics P1 (algebra, patterns, functions, finance and probability), November 2024 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers transcribed from the rendered pages of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf); the text layer does not hold usable equations. Notation:
^ for powers, sqrt() for roots, a/b for fractions, decimal commas as printed. memo_answer is the
guideline's final answer and memo_working its working (tick marks and mark descriptors left out).
The guideline is bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. Graphs and diagrams are described
in brackets in the question text. The information sheet printed with the paper is not transcribed.
FORMAT: 150 marks, 3 hours, ten compulsory questions (Q1 26, Q2 17, Q3 11, Q4 15, Q5 17, Q6 16,

subject: Maths

questions.memo_note: The guideline's mark column prints x = -4; the working gives x = 4.

questions.text: 2x^2 - 3x = 7 (answers correct to TWO decimal places)
questions.topic: Equations: quadratic formula and completing the square
questions.memo_working: 2x^2 - 3x - 7 = 0; x = (-(-3) ± sqrt((-3)^2 - 4(2)(-7)))/(2(2)). Penalise 1 mark for incorrect rounding.

questions.text: (x + 1)(4 - x) > 0 ; where x ∈ N
questions.memo_working: (x + 1)(x - 4) < 0; critical values x = -1 or x = 4; -1 < x < 4 but x ∈ N

questions.text: Solve for p
Hence, or otherwise, solve for x if 14/sqrt(x + 5) = sqrt(x + 5) + 5
questions.memo_working: let sqrt(x + 5) = p: 2 = sqrt(x + 5) or -7 = sqrt(x + 5); but -7 ≠ sqrt(x + 5); x + 5 = (2)^2; x = 4 - 5

questions.text: Solve for x and y simultaneously: -3y = 1 - x and x^2 - 2xy - y^2 - 7 = 0
questions.topic: Equations: simultaneous equations (one linear, one quadratic)
questions.memo_note: Official answer kept. The guideline divides 2y^2 + 4y - 6 = 0 to y^2 - 2y - 3 = 0; it should be y^2 + 2y - 3 = 0, (y + 3)(y - 1) = 0, giving x = 4, y = 1 or x = -8, y = -3 (both satisfy the original equations; x = 10, y = 3 does not).

questions.text: If 2x^(-1) + x^(-2) = 3 and x < 0, determine, without using a calculator, the value of 2(6x - 1)^(-1).
Simplify fully, without using a calculator: (sqrt(32) - sqrt(18) + 3sqrt(3)) / (sqrt(108) + sqrt(8))
Calculate a possible value for a^2 + b^2, if it is given that a and b are rational numbers such that sqrt(a) + sqrt(b) = sqrt(9 + sqrt(56)).
questions.memo_working: square both sides: a + b + 2sqrt(ab) = 9 + 2sqrt(14) (sqrt(56) = 2sqrt(14)); a + b = 9 and ab = 14; a = 2 and b = 7 (or a = 7, b = 2); 2^2 + 7^2 = 53

questions.context: QUESTION 3 | 3.1 Consider the linear number pattern: -5 ; -9 ; -13 ; ...
questions.text: Write down the next TWO terms of the pattern.
Determine an expression for the nth term of the pattern.
Calculate the value of n for which Tn = -141.

In a linear number pattern the first term is x and a common difference is 5 less than the first term. Calculate the value of the first term if it is given that the sum of the first three terms of the linear number pattern is 63.
Show that the above number pattern is quadratic.
questions.memo_answer: First differences -14 ; -10 ; -6; second differences 4 ; 4 (constant), so the pattern is quadratic.

questions.text: Determine the nth term of the quadratic number pattern in the form, Tn = an^2 + bn + c.
questions.memo_note: The guideline's mark column prints a = 6, b = -9, c = 6; the working and final answer give 2, -20 and 42.

questions.text: Calculate the value of T52.
Determine the smallest value of the quadratic number pattern.
Determine the value(s) of n for which the terms of the quadratic number pattern will be positive.
questions.memo_working: 2n^2 - 20n + 42 > 0; n^2 - 10n + 21 > 0; (n - 7)(n - 3) > 0; critical values 3 and 7 (also accepted: 1 ≤ n ≤ 2 or n ≥ 8)

questions.context: QUESTION 5 | The lines y = -x + 4 and y = x - 2 are the axes of symmetry of the function f(x) = -3/(x + p) + q.
questions.text: Show that p = -3 and q = 1.
Calculate the x-intercept of f.
Calculate the y-intercept of f.
Sketch the graph of f. Clearly label all intercepts with the axes and asymptotes.
questions.memo_answer: Hyperbola with dashed asymptotes x = 3 and y = 1, branches in the second and fourth quadrants relative to the asymptotes: the left branch passes through (0 ; 2) and rises towards x = 3; the right branch comes up from below next to x = 3 and passes through (6 ; 0) towards y = 1 (marks: shape, asymptotes, intercepts).

questions.text: Write down the domain of g if g is the reflection of f along the line x = 0.
For which values of x will x.f(x) ≤ 0?

questions.text: Determine the value of f(6).

Write down the equation of g in the form g(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, if it is given that g(x) is obtained by shifting f(x) two units to the right and five units up.
questions.memo_note: Official answer kept; the expansion x^2 - 4x + 4 - 4x + 8 - 5 + 5 gives x^2 - 8x + 12.

questions.text: Suppose h is a tangent, to the curve f at a certain point, with a gradient of -2. Calculate the y-intercept of h.
For which values of k will f(x) - k = 0 have just one real root?
questions.memo_working: turning point x = -(-4)/(2(1)) = 2, f(2) = -9; on the restricted domain the line y = k cuts f once at the turning point or above the end point (6 ; 7)

questions.context: QUESTION 7 | The graphs of f(x) = -(b)^x + 8 and g(x) = (3/2)x + 7 are drawn below. A(-2 ; 4) and B are points of intersection of f and g. B is the y-intercept of both graphs f and g. [Graph: f increases towards the dashed asymptote above B; the straight line g passes through A and B.]
questions.text: Write down the coordinates of B.

questions.memo_working: A and B also lie on g, gradient 3/2

questions.text: Write down the equation of the asymptote of f.
Calculate the vertical distance between f and g at x = -1.
Describe the transformation of f to h if h(x) = (1/2)^x - 5.
questions.memo_answer: Reflection along the x-axis, then a vertical translation of 3 units upwards.

questions.context: 8.2 Koza deposits R15 000 into a bank account for a period of 10 years. The interest rate for the first four years is 6% per annum compounded monthly. For the next six years, the interest rate changes to 10% per annum compounded semi-annually.
questions.text: Convert the nominal rates to annual effective rates. (Answers correct to FOUR decimal places)
Hence, use the effective rates or otherwise, calculate the future value of the savings at the end of the ten-year period.

The interest rate for the first 4 years remains at 6% p.a. compounded monthly. For the next 2 years the interest rate is x% p.a. compounded quarterly. For the last 4 years the interest rate is x% p.a. compounded semi-annually. If Koza receives R48 897,03 at the end of the 10-year period, determine the interest rate for the last 6 years, i.e. the value of x.

questions.context: QUESTION 9 | 9.1 A certain company uses a camera detector system to detect trespassers. Two independent cameras, A and B are installed, one at the front main gate and the other one at the back of the building. If someone trespasses, the probability that the person will be detected by camera A is 0,5 and the probability that the person will be detected by camera B is 0,6.
questions.text: If there is a trespasser, what is the probability that the trespasser will be detected by at least one camera?
Determine the probability that the trespasser will not be detected.

questions.context: 9.2 At a certain high school, a survey was carried out on 110 learners, about their subject choices. The Venn diagram shows the results of the survey in terms of: • Mathematics (M) • Physical Sciences (P) • Accounting (A) [Venn diagram: M only 26; M and P only 9; P only 24; M and A only 12; M, P and A x; P and A only 4; A only 15; none 12.]
questions.text: Show that x = 8.
Calculate the probability that a learner chosen at random does only one of the three subjects.
Calculate the probability that a learner chosen at random does Mathematics and Accounting, but not Physical Sciences.

Bennie has two fair spinners. (Circles are divided into 3 and 8 equal parts, respectively) [SPINNER 1: three equal sectors RED, BLUE and GREEN. SPINNER 2: eight equal sectors, 3 RED and 5 BLUE.] Bennie is going to spin both spinners. What is the probability that it lands on the same colour after spinning each spinner once?
questions.topic: Probability: tree diagrams and contingency tables
questions.memo_working: tree diagram: R, B, G each 1/3 on spinner 1, then B 5/8 and R 3/8 on spinner 2; P(B ; B) = 1/3 × 5/8 = 5/24; P(R ; R) = 1/3 × 3/8 = 1/8; 5/24 + 1/8 = 1/3
